title.narrative: UNDP Pilot Treaties Programme- Implementation of AU Treaties, 2018-2023
UNDP Pilot Treaties Programme-Implementation of AU Treaties (2018-2023)

description.narrative: The intervention is designed to address the challenges and bottlenecks associated with ratification and domestication of African treaties of key importance primarily within the fields of democracy, gender equality and human rights thereby help enhancing the capacity of the AU to be able to manage the ratification process, and to provide tailored support to Member States with domestication and implementation related challenges. This is expected to increase ratification and domestication rates of those selected AU treaties in six selected Member States and thereby help African Union and RECs deliver on their mandate, especially cross-cutting issues related to resilience-building. In order to systematically tackle the challenges the intervention proposed a multi- pronged intervention, i.e., with regional, sub-regional and national actors.

Insatsen avser stöd till en komponent inom UNDPs regionala Afrika-program med syfte att påskynda ratificering och implementering av sex konventioner antagna inom Afrikanska Unionen (AU) med fokus på mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati, god samhällsstyrning samt jämställdhet.
Föreliggande förslag rör en pilotfas om tre år, för att utveckla metoder, testa realismen i angreppssättet och utvärdera konkreta resultat innan en fullskalig fortsättning utarbetas. Pilotfasen inleds med en startfas om ett år då bl.a. samordningsmekanismer, baslinjer, mål och indikatorer till resultatramverket ska utvecklas och fastställas.
Insatsen avser att stödja ratificerings- och implementeringsprocessen genom fem samordnade aktivitetslinjer: -Stärka kapaciteten hos AU-kommissionens juridiska enhet så att denna bättre ska kunna stödja medlemsstaterna. -Harmonisera processer for lagstiftning och ratificering mellan AU och tre regionala ekonomiska kommissioner (ECOWAS för Västafrika, EAC för Östafrika och SADC för södra Afrika). -Bygga nationell kapacitet hos utvalda medlemssländer i syfte att påskynda arbetet med att ratificera och implementera antagna konventioner samt för bättre kunskapsöverföring mellan medlemsstaterna. -Ökad kunskap och förståelse hos befolkningen i medlemsländerna gällande antagna konventioner för att bidra till ett medborgarnas ägarskap. -Samordning av nationella aktörer för implementering av konventioner på regional och nationell nivå.
Programmets genomförs gemensamt av AU (AU Legal Office) och UNDP (Regional Bureau for Africa/Reginal Service Centre) i nära samordning med tre Regionala Ekonomiska Gemenskaper (RECs), relevanta nationella myndigheter samt internationella organisationer och CSO-partnerns på nationell nivå.
Programmets totala budget uppgår till 130 milj. kr varav Sida bidrar med maximalt 60 milj. kronor (46% av den totala projektkostnaden). UNDP avser att bidra med 12 milj. kr (9,2%) och det resterande beloppet på 45% är ännu inte finansierat. Samtliga medel kommer att administreras av UNDP och s.k. forwarding of funds förekommer således inte.
Sida, representerad av ambassaden, kommer att vara medlem i en styrgrupp för insatsen med uppgift att föra strategiska diskussioner och ge råd – särskilt angående frågor gällande öppenhet, ansvarsutkrävande, uppföljning och utvärdering, resultatstyrning, kvalitetskontroll samt riskhantering.

This initiative concerns support for the UNDP Regional Africa Programme that aims at promoting better ratification and domestication of six selected AU treaties, mainly in the area of human rights, democracy, good governance and gender, in five African countries.
The present proposal constitutes a pilot phase covering a period of three years, during which methods will be developed, the realism of the approach will be tested and an evaluation will be performed in order to define results and challenges prior to the elaboration of a full-scale implementation program. The pilot phase is initiated by a starting-up period of 1 year (the inception phase) when coordinating mechanisms, baselines,targets and indicators will be developed and agreed upon.
The intervention aims at addressing the challenges and bottlenecks associated with ratification and domestication of AU treaties through the following five multi-layered and integrated causal mechanisms:
1. Strengthening capacities of the AUC Office of Legal Counsel to build a support structure for Member States. 2. Harmonizing regional approaches to continental law-making and ratification amongst the AU and RECs. 3. Building national capacities for ratification and domestication, and enhancing knowledge exchange/peer support. 4. Public awareness-raising at the regional and national levels to ensure AU treaties and protocols are understood and owned by the public. 5. Alignment with development actors at the national and regional levels.
The intervention will be realized through a Joint AU-UNDP Programme, implemented between the AUC Office of Legal Counsel and UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Africa (RBA) represented with its Regional Service Centre (RSC) in Addis Ababa, in close collaboration and coordination with RECs, national governments, international development partners, and other relevant partners at the national level.
The total budget that is required for the full implementation of the programme is 130 MSEK and the maximum amount that the Embassy plans to contribute is 60 MSK, which is around 46 % of the total project cost. Out of the remaining uncovered 70 MSEK (53.8%) UNDP plans to cover 12 MSEK (9.2%). The remaining 58 MSEK, which is around 44.6% of the total project cost, remains to be uncovered from any other funding source. No fund is going to be forwarded to any other organization, i.e. the entire fund will be managed by UNDP.
Sida will be part of the Programme oversight Board that will serve as a strategic advisory mechanism to deliver on institutional effectiveness- especially on transparency, accountability, monitoring and evaluation, overall RBM, quality assurance and risk management.

The project focused on addressing critical areas such as human rights, governance, women's rights, child protection, youth empowermment, and anticorruption across six pilot countries: Kenya, Mozambique, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Tunisia. It has made some strides in addressing systemic gaps in legal and institutional frameworks in these nations.
The project reports that, in measurable terms, key achievements by treaty include increase in judicial reliance on the African Charter on Human and People's Rights (ACHPR) in Kenya, alongside broader improvements in human rights protections, especially in Kenya and Tunisia. For example in Kenya, the project supported the digitization of judicial services, making human rights cases more accesible through platform like Judicial efiling system. This resulted from judicial reforms and the integration of ACHPR provisions into national legal systems, which enhanced public access to justice. In Mozambique and Sao Tome and Principe, reforms facilitated by the project strengthened legal protections against genderbased violence (GBV), and Kenya made notable progress in gender equity in employment and education through establishment of National Gender and Equality Commission (NGEC) in 2020. In Mozambique, the project played significant role in reinforcing initially passed (2009) Law Against Domestic Violence. The project reports that the these initiatives led to 35% increase in legal protections for women, coupled with enhanced reporting and prosecution of GBV cases.
On the African Youth Charter, the project reports to have yielded improvements in youth participation in governance and employment, particularly in Kenya, Senegal and Mozambique. Through the support of the project, Youth councils were established, and entrepreneurship programs such as Youth Enterprise Development Fund (in Kenya) and PSEYouth Plan (in Senegal) established.
These efforts contributed to a 25% increase in youth employment in Kenya. With regards to Child Protection, Burkina and Sao Tome and Principe strengthened their legal frameworks through adoption of child laws (2019 in Sao Tome and 2020 in Burkina Faso) and nationwide awareness programms aimed at reducing child labor and increasing school attendance. Tunisia improved its juvenile legal frameworks focusing on rehabilitation over punishment. This has led to school enrollment increase by 30% in Sao Tome and Principe and the project reports a notable reduction in child labor.
Prior to the project, weaknesses in the electoral management systems of the pilot countries were mapped. Then legal reforms targeting these countries were designed. In Mozambique and Kenya, the project targeted the democratic institutions and enhancing electoral integrity. In Kenya, the project provided support to adoption of Election Laws (Amendment) Act 2016 which introduced stricter regulations for vote tallying and use of technology in elections. Sao Tome and Principe institutionalized democratic practices by establishing independent electoral bodies and adopting legislation to ensure free and fair elections. The project reports that this has contributed to more peaceful elections and 20% increase in electoral credibility. In the anticorruption domain, Kenya and Mozambique made strides in anticorruption reforms by strengthening anticorruption frameworks and enhancing transparency. The project supported digitization of anticorruption reporting systems, including the EACC (Ethics and AntiCorruption Commission) Online Portal that was launched in 2020 in Kenya. The platform allows citizens to report corrupt practices annonymously. Further, the project provided capacity building initiatives for law enforcement and judicial officers improving prosecution of corruption cases. In Mozambique, the project supported integration of digital financial management systems in 2021, enhancing transaprency in public sector transactions and In Burkina Faso, the project supported introduction of whisteleblower protection laws in 2020 enforcement remains a challenge due to political instability and security issues. These efforts is reported to have contributed to a increase in asset recovery in Kenya, signaling stronger enforcement of anticorruption laws.
The project established National Sectoral Committees in four countries (Kenya, Sao Tome and Principe, Mozambique and Burkina Faso) to monitor Member States' commitment to regional and global frameworks. In Kenya, the President is now required to annually report on the nation's progress in implementing global commitments. The coordination mechanisms (NSC) gather themain stakeholders in the process of ratification and implementation of international conventions, such as the sectoral ministries and parliaments. As these bodies have been established recently (end of 2023), the outcome of their action is yet to be observed.
The project also redesigned the AU Treaty Webpage, and completed some Treaties Archiving platforms for some Governments. However, most of these products cannot be found centrally on the UNDP public web pages on the AU treaties. Furthermore, the Communication Strategy was issued at the end of the project cycle, and with no dedicated staff. This leads the project review to conclude that some of these products have not been used and disseminated as they could have been. UNDP has informed that the there will be an official launch of the treatys webpage and formal closure of the projet but no date has been provided yet.
The external evaluation from June 2024 concluded that significant capacity was built during the course of the programme and resulted in the ratification of 22 additional treaties since 2019. In particular, it is noted that the programme supported the ratification of seven treaties in Sao Tome and Principe, one treaty in Tunisia, and three treaties in Kenya, where the ACDEG ratification was directed supported by the project. The programme was found to also have produced important knowledge and research products, practical tools and toolkits, training materials, and communication products like press articles, animated videos, etc.
Measuring the impact was not one of the criteria for the evaluation, however, a number of results can according to the evaluation report reasonably be attributed to the project, including those related to the AUC support for treaty processes, strengthening of Member States' ability to ratify and implement treaties, and the citizen awareness raising and demand for compliance.
The evaluation also concluded that interventions at country and regional institutional levels have been relevant for the three outputs of the project. Furthermore, interventions had the merit to address challenges and bottlenecks related to low level of ratification, domestication, and implementation of AU Treaties. The project also helped to monitor Member States' commitments to regional and global frameworks, thanks to the establishment of National Sectoral Committees. At the regional level however, there was a low level of regional ownership and weak coordination between regional institutions, namely the AU Commission and the Regional Economic Commissions.
Nonetheless, in terms of monitoring results, beyond the Annual Work Plans, the evaluation found that there was a lack of a systematically updated M&E Framework based on the programme Results Framework. Stronger indicators, baselines and targets would have helped measure progress in results.
The Embassy agrees with the evaluation in that both the pandemic and the fact that the programme was centrally managed limited the full implementation and created limitations and delays at field level. Nonetheless, once these two issues were improved, the execution made more progress in 2022 and 2023.
The evaluation concluded that the programme outputs were generally achieved but that the process of change, however, will take more time to unfold. The Embassy has several times questioned UNDP's own result reporting in terms of attribution as the reporting often time seemed inflated.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
